goals: Work is queued durably and performed by workers with a retry schedule.

No business logic in the HTTP layer.
Every component logs one structured line per unit of work with the correlation id.
No in-process state that a second instance would not see; instances are interchangeable.

Python 3.12 as stated in the constraints.
Stateless processes: configuration from the environment, no local files that a second instance would not see.
definition_of_done: Acceptance checks of the package pass.
No file outside the write scope changed.
Every public operation of the implemented interfaces exists with the declared inputs.

components.name: Store
components.responsibility: Owns persistence of the domain entities: durable writes, reads, listing, and the schema/migrations.

components.name: Work queue
components.responsibility: Durable, ordered hand-off of work items between the ingest path and the workers, with visibility timeout and dead-letter.

components.name: Audit log
components.responsibility: Append-only record of who did what to which resource, queryable by resource and actor.

components.name: Domain core
components.responsibility: Business rules and validation for the domain entities; the only module that changes state through the store.

components.name: Outbound HTTP client
components.responsibility: Performs the outbound HTTP call with timeouts, size limits, redirect and private-address protection, and returns a classified outcome.

components.name: Notifier
components.responsibility: Sends operator/customer notifications through the configured channel with templating and rate limiting.

components.name: Observability
components.responsibility: Metrics registry and exposition, structured logging, health/readiness endpoints.

components.name: Authentication
components.responsibility: Authenticates callers and resolves them to a principal and scope; enforces authorization for management operations.

components.name: Import/export
components.responsibility: Streams records to and from CSV/JSON with validation and partial-failure reporting.

components.name: Worker

components.name: Scheduler

components.name: Batch job

decisions.title: Work queue technology
decisions.context: Work items must survive a crash and be leased by several workers.

options.name: PostgreSQL table with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
pros: transactional with the domain data (persist + enqueue atomically)
cons: throughput bounded by the database (fine to ~10k items/s)

options.name: Redis Streams with consumer groups
pros: built-in consumer groups and pending lists
cons: separate from the transactional store: needs an outbox

options.name: Managed broker (SQS/RabbitMQ/Kafka)
cons: at-least-once semantics still need an outbox

decisions.choice: PostgreSQL table with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 1.0). PostgreSQL table with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP: 2.15; Redis Streams with consumer groups: unavailable (needs redis, not in the constraints); Managed broker: unavailable (needs broker, not in the constraints); In-memory queue: unavailable (ruled out by durable_required)

decisions.title: Where delayed retries wait
decisions.context: Failed deliveries must run again at a computed future time.

options.name: not_before column on the work item; the scheduler promotes due rows
pros: one durable store for queued and delayed items
trivial to inspect and to redeliver manually

options.name: Redis sorted set keyed by due time
cons: a second store to keep consistent

decisions.choice: not_before column on the work item; the scheduler promotes due rows
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 1.0). not_before column on the work item: 2.01; Redis sorted set keyed by due time: unavailable (needs redis, not in the constraints); In-process timers: unavailable (ruled out by durable_required)

decisions.title: Process topology
decisions.context: The same code base serves requests and performs background work.

options.name: One image, role by flag: `api` and `worker` processes scale independently
pros: independent scaling of ingress and outbound work

options.name: Single process with background threads
cons: request latency competes with outbound work

options.name: Separate services per concern (ingest, admin, delivery)
cons: three deployables for a team of three

decisions.choice: One image, role by flag: `api` and `worker` processes scale independently
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 1.0). One image, role by flag: `api` and `worker` proc: 2.00; Separate services per concern: 1.59; Single process with background threads: 1.39
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Separate services per concern' gives up: clear ownership. Not choosing 'Single process with background threads' gives up: one deployable.

decisions.title: Outbound request safety
decisions.context: The system makes HTTP requests to customer-supplied URLs.

options.name: Resolve and block private/link-local ranges; pin the resolved IP; cap body size and redirects; per-request timeout
Plain HTTP client with a timeout

decisions.choice: Plain HTTP client with a timeout
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 1.0). Plain HTTP client with a timeout: 1.25; Resolve and block private/link-local ranges: 1.13
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Resolve and block private/link-local ranges; pin' gives up: closes SSRF and slow-loris classes.

decisions.title: Primary store
decisions.context: Domain records need durable, queryable storage.

options.name: MySQL / MariaDB (the stated database)
cons: weaker JSON and DDL ergonomics than PostgreSQL

options.name: Redis for the hot state (as stated) with a relational store for durable records
pros: the stated home of the hot data

options.name: Managed document store (DynamoDB/MongoDB, as stated)
cons: query patterns must be designed up front

decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 1.0). PostgreSQL: 2.56; SQLite: 1.69; Files: 1.11; MySQL / MariaDB: unavailable (needs mysql, not in the constraints); Redis for the hot state: unavailable (needs redis_primary, not in the constraints); Managed document store: unavailable (needs document_db, not in the constraints); In-memory: unavailable (ruled out by durable_required). chosen in the interview
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'SQLite' gives up: zero operations, single file. Not choosing 'Files' gives up: no dependencies, human readable.

decisions.title: Caller authentication
decisions.context: Management operations must be attributable to a customer or operator.

options.name: API keys per customer, hashed at rest, sent as a bearer token
cons: no delegation or expiry unless added

options.name: OAuth2 / OIDC with the platform's identity provider
Session tokens issued by the platform's own account service to game/mobile clients (device-bound, short-lived, refreshable)
No account: a reference number plus a knowledge factor (date of birth) resumes a saved application; every attempt rate-limited and logged
pros: no credentials to manage for occasional users
cons: a reference number can be shared; scope what it unlocks

options.name: Email one-time code / magic link (no account needed)

decisions.choice: API keys per customer, hashed at rest, sent as a bearer token
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 1.0). API keys per customer, hashed at rest, sent as a: 1.25; Mutual TLS: 0.87; OAuth2 / OIDC with the platform's identity provi: unavailable (needs idp, not in the constraints); Session tokens issued by the platform's own acco: unavailable (needs game_client, not in the constraints); No account: a reference number plus a knowledge : unavailable (needs no_account_auth, not in the constraints); Email one-time code / magic link: unavailable (needs email_auth, not in the constraints). chosen in the interview
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Mutual TLS' gives up: strong, no secrets in headers.

decisions.title: Redundancy for the availability target
decisions.context: The availability target must be met through instance failures and deploys.

options.name: Two or more interchangeable instances per role behind the ingress, health checks, rolling deploys
cons: needs stateless instances and a shared store

decisions.choice: Two or more interchangeable instances per role behind the ingress, health checks, rolling deploys
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 1.0). Two or more interchangeable instances per role b: 1.72; Active-active across two regions: 1.47; Single instance with health-based restart: 1.25
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Active-active across two regions' gives up: survives a regional outage. Not choosing 'Single instance with health-based restart' gives up: simplest, cheapest.

risks.description: At-least-once delivery means a target can receive the same event twice (crash between call and ack).
risks.mitigation: Send a stable event id and attempt number in headers; document idempotent consumption; never retry on 2xx.

risks.description: Many targets fail at once (regional outage) and their retries align, creating a burst.
risks.mitigation: Add jitter to the backoff schedule and cap concurrent deliveries per partition and globally.

risks.description: Customer-supplied URLs can point at internal addresses or metadata services.
risks.mitigation: Resolve before connecting, block private ranges, pin the IP, forbid redirects to non-public hosts.

risks.description: Retried and dead-lettered items accumulate and slow the lease query.
risks.mitigation: Partial index on (partition, not_before) for live items; archive terminal items on a schedule.

risks.description: Timestamp-based signatures and not_before scheduling depend on wall clocks.
risks.mitigation: Use the database clock for scheduling; tolerate a bounded skew window when verifying timestamps.

risks.description: A widespread failure disables many targets and emails every owner at once.
risks.mitigation: Rate-limit notifications per owner and batch them.

risks.description: A management operation reachable without authentication.
risks.mitigation: Authenticate in one middleware for every management route; test every route unauthenticated.

risks.description: Entities evolve; migrations run against live data.
risks.mitigation: Versioned migrations applied before deploy; additive changes first, removals one release later.

risks.description: Payloads or uploads without size limits exhaust memory or disk.
risks.mitigation: Enforce size limits at the surface; reject early with a clear error.

risks.description: [tampering] Store: Injection through query construction.
risks.mitigation: Parameterised queries only; no string-built SQL. Check: static check for string-formatted SQL finds nothing

risks.description: [information_disclosure] Store: Backups and dumps contain everything.
risks.mitigation: Encrypt backups; restrict who can take them. Check: backup file is not readable without the key

risks.description: [denial_of_service] Work queue: A poison item is retried forever and blocks its partition.
risks.mitigation: Attempt cap and dead-letter; per-partition concurrency cap. Check: an always-failing item ends in the dead-letter after the cap

risks.description: [tampering] Work queue: Items are processed twice after a crash between call and ack.
risks.mitigation: Idempotent processing with the item id; ack only after the outcome is recorded. Check: kill the worker mid-call; the item is redelivered exactly once more

risks.description: [ssrf] Outbound HTTP client: A customer-supplied URL points at internal or metadata addresses.
risks.mitigation: Resolve and block private/link-local ranges; pin the resolved IP; forbid redirects to non-public hosts. Check: URL to 169.254.169.254 / 10.0.0.1 / localhost is refused before connecting

risks.description: [denial_of_service] Outbound HTTP client: A slow or infinite response body ties up a worker.
risks.mitigation: Per-request timeout; cap response size; stream and discard bodies. Check: target that stalls is cut at the timeout; 100 MB body is cut at the cap

risks.description: [information_disclosure] Outbound HTTP client: Secrets or internal headers leak to targets.
risks.mitigation: Send only the documented headers; never forward inbound headers. Check: captured request has exactly the documented headers

risks.description: [denial_of_service] Notifier: Notification storms and template injection.
risks.mitigation: Rate-limit per recipient; escape template context. Check: 1,000 failures produce one digest per owner

risks.description: [spoofing] Authentication: Credential stuffing or leaked keys.
risks.mitigation: Hash keys at rest; allow revocation; rate-limit failures. Check: revoked key is rejected within seconds; brute force is throttled

risks.description: [elevation] Authentication: A caller acts on another tenant's resources.
risks.mitigation: Every core operation takes the principal and checks ownership. Check: cross-tenant request returns 404/403 for every operation

risks.description: [spoofing] Public HTTP API: Requests without a verified caller identity reach domain operations.
risks.mitigation: Authenticate every route in one middleware; deny by default. Check: every route returns 401 without credentials

risks.description: [tampering] Public HTTP API: Malformed or oversized bodies reach the core.
risks.mitigation: Schema-validate and size-limit at the surface; reject before parsing fully. Check: fuzz the body; oversize returns 413

risks.description: [denial_of_service] Public HTTP API: A single caller saturates the service.
risks.mitigation: Per-caller rate limit and request timeouts. Check: burst from one key returns 429; others unaffected

risks.description: [information_disclosure] Public HTTP API: Stack traces or internal ids leak in error responses.
risks.mitigation: Map exceptions to fixed error shapes; log details server-side only. Check: no traceback text in any 4xx/5xx body
